governed_construct: A typed position in TypeScript source: every declared binding (variable, parameter, property, return) and every explicit type annotation, type assertion, type argument or type-parameter default. One instance per such position; it conforms when its resolved type is not, and does not contain, `any`.
interpretation: The rule forbids letting a value or type be `any` where proper typing is possible. A unit violates it if any typed position resolves (per the TypeScript type checker) to `any` or contains `any` as a component: explicit `any` keywords (annotations, `as any`, `any[]`, `Record<string, any>`, `Promise<any>`, generic defaults `T = any`), parameters with no annotation and no contextual type (implicit any), and type aliases/annotations that resolve to `any` through other types (e.g. `ReturnType<typeof JSON.parse>`). `unknown` with narrowing, generics, unions and concrete interfaces conform. The word `any` in comments or string literals is irrelevant. Contextually typed callback parameters (e.g. `forEach((h) => ...)` on a typed array) are not implicit any. A file with no declarations or type positions (e.g. a pure re-export barrel) is NOT_APPLICABLE. Unresolved external types are avoided in fixtures so verdicts do not hinge on missing packages.
